newsitem.title: USA: BOJ acknowledges fall in long-term rates.
newsitem.headline: BOJ acknowledges fall in long-term rates.

text.p: The Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said the recent fall in long-term interest rates may be reflecting changes in sentiment about Japan's economic prospects.

Asked whether the BOJ thought the recent fall in Japan's long-term interest rates reflected economic fundamentals, Matsushita said: "Long-term interest rates have previously reflected expectations of stronger economic prospects but some changes have been seen recently, in accordance with conditions."

Japan's long-term interest rates fell below three percent to around 2.7 percent last week. There were media reports that the BOJ showed concern that the decline was excessive and not in line with the state of the Japanese economy, which was recovering gradually.

Matsushita also welcomed the Group of 10 agreement on the International Monetary Fund's New Agreement to Borrow (NAB). He said it was "significant" that new and emerging countries of Asia were joining in the creation of new international monetary systems.
"It was a meeting which bore much fruit," he said.
Takacoshi Kato, vice finance minister for international affairs, also welcomed the G10 agreement on NAB as well as the IMF interim committee progress on talks over SDR allocations.
"I think there indeed was lots of progress," he said.
